name: The Beaumont
insider_take: This Art Deco masterpiece in Mayfair feels like stepping into a sophisticated 1920s novel, where classic British elegance meets modern luxury.
whats_special: The Beaumont occupies a stunning 1926 Art Deco building that was originally designed by renowned architects Wimperis, Simpson and Guthrie. The hotel's pièce de résistance is ROOM, a living sculpture by Antony Gormley perched on the facade - it's actually a bookable suite where guests sleep inside a work of art. The hotel sits in the heart of Mayfair, just steps from Bond Street's luxury shopping and some of London's finest galleries.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea in the hotel's elegant lounge - it's consistently ranked among London's best and you'll avoid the tourist crowds at other famous venues.
dont_miss: The Colony Grill Room, helmed by acclaimed chef Jason Atherton, serves exceptional modern American cuisine in an intimate setting. Take a stroll through nearby Mount Street, one of London's most charming Georgian streets, and explore the hidden gem of Mount Street Gardens - a peaceful Victorian garden square that most tourists never discover.
pros: Art Deco elegance with 1920s glamour and sophisticated design
Prime Mayfair location near Oxford Street and Bond Street shopping
Exceptional service with personalized attention and refined hospitality
Acclaimed Colony Grill Room restaurant and stylish American Bar
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive Mayfair positioning
Intimate boutique size with limited room inventory
